mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has collapsed from -24.3% to -37.3% then recovered to -21.9%, signaling volatile employment patterns. This instability suppresses consumer confidence and discretionary spending, driving RETAIL_REC further negative over the next four weeks as households prioritize essential goods.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined 12.4 points week t-2w to t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the mean of the last 28 days, or WORKPLACES stabilizes above -15% for two consecutive weeks without RETAIL_REC declining.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has recovered from -6.7% to 0.0% at t-0w, indicating households are normalizing essential shopping trips. This normalization of baseline provisioning behavior frees discretionary budget and time for retail-and-recreation visits, producing a positive shift in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses above -3% in any week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at 0.0% at t-0w, highest in snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or remains flat over the next 14 days despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining at or above -2%, or GROCERY_PHARM reverts below -5%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT stations show persistent suppression (-31.6% to -38.9% range), indicating restricted mobility infrastructure. When transit access remains constrained, retail-and-recreation venues dependent on public transport access experience lower footfall, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed relative to the baseline period.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -30% for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT below -30% in all four weeks of snapshot
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -20% and RETAIL_REC does not decline over the following four weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises despite TRANSIT remaining below -30%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has declined from -10.4% to -20.9%, while RESIDENTIAL has risen from 9.9% to 13.0%, indicating households are retreating indoors. This shift reflects risk-averse behavior that suppresses discretionary retail visits. The divergence between outdoor and indoor confinement predicts continued RETAIL_REC decline as behavioral caution persists.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines more than 5 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL rises simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell 6.5 points from t-2w to t-1w
fact:RESIDENTIAL rose 3.0 points from t-2w to t-1w
failure_condition: PARKS and RESIDENTIAL trends reverse (PARKS rises, RESIDENTIAL falls) within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises despite the interaction signal persisting.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT suppression (-31.6% at t-0w) combined with WORKPLACES weakness (-21.9%) indicates policy-driven mobility constraints remain in force. Under sustained policy restriction, retail venues cannot recover footfall. RETAIL_REC will remain depressed unless both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES recover above -15% simultaneously, signaling policy relaxation.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below -20% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -31.6% and WORKPLACES at -21.9% at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -20% over the next four weeks while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain below -20%, or policy indicators (TRANSIT and WORKPLACES) recover above -15% without RETAIL_REC improving.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has stabilized around -27% to -29% over the last three weeks (t-3w to t-1w), with only minor weekly variance. This plateau suggests the current regime has reached an equilibrium state. Absent exogenous shocks, RETAIL_REC will persist near this equilibrium level over the next four weeks, producing a direction of zero or minimal change.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC variance of 4.7 points across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -20% or falls below -35% over the next four weeks, indicating the equilibrium has been disrupted by an unobserved shock.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM recovery to 0.0% at t-0w signals that essential-goods shopping has normalized. When essential shopping normalizes, households redirect attention to deferred retail-and-recreation consumption. This pent-up demand effect will drive RETAIL_REC positive over the next two weeks as the behavioral shift propagates.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM reaches 0% or above while RETAIL_REC remains below -25%
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at 0.0% and RETAIL_REC at -27.9% at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve by more than 3 points within two weeks of GROCERY_PHARM reaching 0%, or GROCERY_PHARM reverts below -3% before RETAIL_REC shows sustained improvement.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL confinement has increased from 9.9% to 13.0% over the snapshot period, while RETAIL_REC has remained persistently negative. This sustained indoor shift reflects heightened risk aversion. If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated above 12% for the next week, households will continue avoiding retail venues, keeping RETAIL_REC below -25% over the four-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 12% in the first week of the forecast period
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at 13.0% at t-0w, highest in snapshot
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below 10% within one week and RETAIL_REC subsequently rises above -20% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above 12%.
